chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What do you say about a man who gives his slave one thousand dirhams, or less or more, and says: “Release me from my beating you, or from everything that came from me toward you, or from that by which I frightened and intimidated you”? So he releases him and places him in absolution, desiring what he gave him. Then later the master finds the dirhams that he gave him in a place where the slave had put them, and the master takes them. Are they lawful for him?

So he said: “No.” I said to him: Is not the slave and his property for his master? He said: “This is not that case.” Then he عليه السلام said: “Tell him to return them to him, for it is not lawful for him. For he ransomed himself with them from the slave, out of fear of punishment and retribution on the Day of Judgment.”
I said to him: Then is the slave required to pay zakat on it when a year passes over it? He said: “No, unless he puts it to work with it. And the slave is not given anything from zakat.”

key_terms.افْتَدَى: He ransomed or redeemed himself by means of payment.
key_terms.حَلِّلْنِي: Release me from liability and grant me absolution for wrongdoing.
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: In a state of being absolved or free from claim.
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: The Day of Judgment when final accountability occurs.

ai.seo_question: Can a master take back money given to a slave in exchange for forgiveness, and is zakat due on it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that money given by a master to his slave in order to obtain pardon for wrongdoing cannot later be taken back. The Imam عليه السلام treats this payment as a form of ransom from liability before Allah, especially in relation to punishment and retribution on the Day of Judgment. It also addresses zakat, stating that the slave does not pay it on this money unless he uses it in productive activity, and that a slave is not given from zakat.
